description: Mode boundary between FORECAST_DEGRADED and EMERGENCY must be precisely defined — the EMS could prematurely declare emergency or miss declaration if triggers are ambiguous
resolution_approach: Explicit numerical trigger thresholds (SOC levels, fuel inventory thresholds, generator-fault codes, forecast-confidence thresholds) defined in Area 1 framework
residual_action: SD-12: Numerical trigger thresholds must be derived from station engineering data and defined in the Objective Specification

description: Dynamic EBR (35%/45%) and terminal SOC requirements (35%/55-65%) must be physically achievable across consecutive low-renewable days — battery capacity may be insufficient without larger diesel compensation
resolution_approach: Area 6 requires multi-day rolling MPC validation against representative worst-case weather sequences
residual_action: SD-07, SD-08: Battery capacity and degradation data needed; engineering validation before PROVISIONAL values become governed policy

description: Renewable utilization target (D09: 50-70% polar-day) and terminal SOC requirements (D12: 55-65% precautionary) may conflict — storage may be needed for reserve rather than renewable integration
resolution_approach: D15 lexicographic ordering resolves this: Stage 2 (reserve maintenance) strictly dominates Stage 4 (renewable utilization). If conflict arises, terminal SOC wins and renewable utilization metric simply reports as not met for that period
residual_action: No new action required — priority ordering is sufficient resolution; KPI reporting must clearly separate reserve compliance from renewable target compliance

description: Fuel budget soft ceiling (D08) and hard Critical reliability requirement (D04) must never be placed in operational conflict — budget exceedance must not force Critical load shedding
resolution_approach: D08 explicitly states the fuel budget is soft-managed and NEVER forces Critical load shedding. Area 5 policy definition preserves this by classifying budget as a soft KPI with governance review triggers, not a hard MILP constraint
residual_action: No new action required — design principle explicitly preserved in Area 5

description: Forecast safety margins (D13: provisional percentages) must be calibrated to avoid systematic over-conservatism that unnecessarily depletes renewable credits or forces excessive diesel use
resolution_approach: Annual review of safety margin percentages against actual station forecast-error statistics (SD-09, SD-10, SD-11) with governance-authorized revision process
residual_action: SD-09, SD-10, SD-11: Historical forecast vs actual statistics required; NS-10: rolling re-optimization interval requires engineering feasibility assessment

description: Equipment protection (battery/generator hardware limits) is identified in D15 stakeholder proposal as distinct from and concurrent with Stage 1 reliability — exact sequencing within the lexicographic formulation must be made explicit
resolution_approach: Area 9 captures equipment protection constraints as concurrent hard constraints alongside Stage 1, not as a separate lexicographic stage — this avoids creating an infeasible Stage ordering when equipment limits and reliability interact
residual_action: NS-05: Solver formulation must explicitly encode battery SOC bounds and generator power limits as hard constraints co-active with Stage 1
